title: Earliest siphuncle-bearing cephalopod from the early Cambrian.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Dryad API metadata for doi:10.5061/dryad.qbzkh18zk (CC0 licence, 3.26 GB total) and its file listing: three zipped TIFF image stacks of 1.04, 1.08 and 1.13 GB (micro-CT scans of specimens Bar297-1, eoceras-7, eoceras-11 at 3.72, 2.72 and 2.04 µm voxel size, per file names) plus a 1,088-byte README.md. The README download via the Dryad API returned 401 Unauthorized, so I did not read it; the TIFF zips exceed the 50 MB cap and were not downloaded.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only (paywalled, not in Europe PMC): a new millimetre-sized fossil species, Eoceras shaanxiense, from the Cambrian Shuijingtuo Formation of South China, described from shell septa and a segmented tube interpreted as a primordial siphuncle (the tube that links shell chambers in cephalopods).

a1_downloadable.note: Dryad record is public under CC0; files listed with sizes. API file download returned 401 (Dryad needs a browser or token), but the dataset is not access-restricted.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked the file listing: the data are raw 3D scan image stacks of individual fossils, with no table and no label column of any kind. Any label would have to be hand-made (e.g. segmenting septa).

a3_inputs_present.note: The scan images themselves are present (three TIFF stacks, per file listing).

a4_units_stated.note: Voxel sizes (3.72, 2.72, 2.04 µm) are in the file names; no measurement table exists to need units.

a5_enough_rows.note: Three scanned specimens (counted in the file listing), far below the ~400 examples needed even for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Fits on disk and could be processed slice by slice, but irrelevant given A2 and A5.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable against full text (paywalled); three specimen scans listed on Dryad.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists; the paper's conclusion (that the tube is a siphuncle) is an expert morphological interpretation, not a measurement.

honest_claim_h3: With three scanned fossils and no labels, no model claim is possible; at most one could test automatic segmentation of shell chambers on these three scans.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use 3D scans of tiny Cambrian shell fossils to automatically identify internal chambers and connecting tubes.
plain_idea.train_on: Micro-CT (X-ray micro-computed tomography) image stacks of fossil shells; 3 specimens verified in the Dryad listing.
plain_idea.predict: A per-voxel mask of septa (internal shell walls) and the segmented tube; no such masks were deposited, so they would have to be drawn by hand.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Automatic segmentation could speed up fossil description, but three specimens cannot train or test such a tool.

ml_idea: None viable: three unlabelled micro-CT scans of a fossil species description.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; project fails Part A on labels and sample size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count specimens in the Dryad listing: 3, done.

verdict_reason: Fossil species description whose only data are three unlabelled micro-CT (3D X-ray) scans totalling 3.26 GB; no label column (A2), three examples (A5), and no measured outcome (A8).
